Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

quam

quam (+ superlative)

quam with a superlative adjective or adverb

as … as possible; as … as possible; quam prīmum, as soon as possible; than

In this lexicon

  • as … as

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 6.7.3: tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe; Cato Agr. 66: quam mundissimē pūrissimēque fīat

  • possible

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.1: quam prīmum; Cic. Fam. 14.14.2: quam saepissimē; Traupman 54, 86

  • than

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 47.2: ēst ille plūs quam capit; Publ. R 24: Rogantī melius quam imperantī pāreās.

  • tam … quam: as … as

    classical

  • ānsa quam manū prehendimus: handhold

    our formation

  • nihil mihi longius est quam ut: look forward to

    classical

  • quam plūrimum: maximum

    classical

  • quam dūdum: when

    classical

  • quam ob rem (quamobrem): why

    classical

Examples

  • nam mellītus erat suamque nōrat ipsam tam bene quam puella mātrem

    for he was sweet as honey, and knew his mistress as well as a little girl knows her motherCatull. 3.6–7

    In the entry for as … as

  • tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe

    all the same, do write as often as you canPlin. Ep. 6.7.3

    In the entry for as … as

  • quam mundissimē pūrissimēque fīat

    let it be done as cleanly and purely as possibleCato Agr. 66

    In the entry for as … as

  • aut quam sīdera multa, cum tacet nox

    or as many as the stars, when the night is silentCatull. 7.7

    In the entry for as … as

  • ego vērō tē quam prīmum, mea vīta, cupiō vidēre

    I want to see you as soon as possible, my darlingCic. Fam. 14.4.1

    In the entry for possible

  • vōs, meae cārissimae animae, quam saepissimē ad mē scrībite

    my dearest hearts, write to me as often as you canCic. Fam. 14.14.2

    In the entry for possible

  • ēst ille plūs quam capit

    he eats more than he can holdSen. Ep. 47.2

    In the entry for than

  • Rogantī melius quam imperantī pāreās.

    One obeys a person who asks better than one who orders.Publ. R 24

    In the entry for than

  • nē plūs cēnseat sapere sē quam dominum

    let him not think he knows more than his masterCato Agr. 5.2

    In the entry for than

  • īnsomnēs magis quam pervigilēs

    sleepless rather than watchfulTac. Ann. 1.65

    In the entry for than

  • nihil enim timidius columbā

    for nothing is more timid than a doveVarr. RR 3.7.4

    In the entry for than

  • quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum, rhombus lātior est tamen patellā

    however wide the dish that holds the turbot, the turbot is wider than the dishMart. 13.81.1–2
